motion.value: 180ms button, field, topic and segmented-view state feedback; CTA expanding layer 240ms and existing arrow shift 180ms; particle track/knob 180ms; Settings knob 180ms and inherited track color 150ms; app nav none; toast 200ms; reduced motion suppresses transitions and animations

motion.name: knowledge-trackball
motion.value: TrackballControls: rotateSpeed 2.1, zoomSpeed 1.1, panSpeed 0.6, dynamicDampingFactor 0.13, staticMoving false, multiTouchRoll true; automatic orbit resumes 2800ms after manual release at 0.035 radians/second.

motion.name: knowledge-focus-flight

cosmicIntegration.authority: local/entry.ts imports inherited cascade through src/cosmic-integration.css, then local/workspace.css; knowledge library.css follows nebula.css.
cosmicIntegration.rendering: Dark shell uses a shared star field; light shell uses blue sky/clouds. Alpha-enabled WebGL remains, with a deliberate deep-space knowledge viewport ground in light and skin-aware toolbar/reader/library.
cosmicIntegration.historical: October light reading-room concepts and November 2 two-night-palette commitment are historical; explicit November 3 user direction supersedes them.

knowledgeVolume.selection: Luminous stellar beacons; sphere meshes have zero opacity and serve only as hit targets.
knowledgeVolume.layout: Overview collapses reading; selecting a node restores the reader. Mathematics and physics remain separate among six domains.
knowledgeVolume.labels: Fitted and farther views hide projected names. Approaching a cloud reveals one title centered exactly on the projected stellar core for all node types. Visibility combines fitted-view zoom ratio, projected core diameter and positive camera depth. Selected labels receive priority; overlapping or reserved/offscreen labels yield locally without relocation or leader lines. Hover text is hidden at a distance and during dragging. The native selector exposes all six domains.
knowledgeVolume.density: Compact fields reduce gas/star and bridge populations below 640px; pixel ratio caps at 1 mobile and 1.3 desktop. Field counts are implementation details, not design tokens.
knowledgeVolume.bridges: Broad irregular XYZ mist and sparse round dust with faded ends represent semantic relations. Random samples and all-axis scatter avoid a narrow centerline; stellar shader marks are round rather than cross-shaped. Near-camera particle opacity fades.
knowledgeVolume.zoom: Selecting a visible node targets its stellar core and fits its contents. Toolbar and wheel zoom share the scene-relative minimum and maximum distances.

localWorkspace.contrast: Light sky-exposed small copy and light knowledge reader content use explicit ink overrides; interior muted text retains its semantic role.
localWorkspace.geometry: 1440px local main; 38px desktop side padding; 760px stacking; 640px five-column local navigation. Scoped 9px fields, 6px chips, 16px library modal and 8px library fields are intentional.

narrative.northStar: 生活阅览室 × 知识宇宙
narrative.overview:
LifeAtlas retains its outlined wordmark, app rail, independent topic index, continuous reading geometry and native controls. The current local workspace extends that world with real record forms, an AI question–references–confirmation–result sequence, readonly mail and local knowledge management. The user's November 3 direction explicitly replaces the earlier pair of night palettes with 深空 · 暗色 (Island, default) and 晴空 · 亮色 (Observatory); stored identifiers remain compatible.

Dark surrounds calm, near-opaque reading surfaces with locally rendered stars. Light surrounds pale navigation and reading surfaces with locally rendered blue sky and clouds. The knowledge map remains a deep-space volume inside light surroundings so stellar knowledge stays visible. This is a code-led expansion of the pinned direction; no new comp or identity replacement is asserted. October white-sheet/lake concepts and the November 2 two-night-palette description are historical, not current authority.
keyCharacteristics: One locally generated atmospheric background: stars in dark, blue sky/clouds in light.
The established LifeAtlas lettering, rail, growth index and continuous reading geometry.
Real local lists and editors, explicit written states and honest empty views.
Chinese sans host UI, serif growth comparisons and local Space Grotesk inside knowledge.
A deep-space 3D knowledge viewport with skin-aware surrounding controls and reading panels.

rules.name: The Textual State Rule
rules.body: Every consequential status has a written label; color is an additional cue.

rules.name: The Continuous Atmosphere Rule
rules.body: Use one body-level atmosphere for the shell; preserve the deliberate dark knowledge viewport in the light skin and skin-aware surrounding reading controls.

rules.name: The Index and Sheet Rule
rules.body: The topic index locates; the near-opaque sheet carries reading. Use dividers and disclosures inside the sheet rather than another stack of equal-weight cards.

rules.name: The Live Task Rule
rules.body: Changing appearance preserves live input, focus, scroll and the current view by updating the document skin attribute.

dos: Do use the active skin's semantic variables and the final local workspace cascade.
Do preserve LifeAtlas lettering, established reading geometry, native control semantics and explicit written states.
Do use ink for small text exposed directly to the light sky and explicit dark reader text on light knowledge surfaces.
Do keep the knowledge viewport deep-space in light mode while its toolbar, reader and library follow the selected skin.
Do keep appearance controls in Settings and honor editing, hidden-document and reduced-motion pauses.
Do distinguish authored local records, isolated test fixtures, bounded rules and user-requested model output.
donts: Don't restore historical lake concepts, a horizontal Observatory desktop shell or the superseded two-dark-palette commitment as current authority.
Don't duplicate brand/navigation inside the knowledge frame or remount live work to change appearance.
Don't put long reading text directly on an animated background.
Don't claim real account success, semantic/vector retrieval, automatic tools, live markets or trading from these surfaces.
Don't treat a simulated analysis or protocol test as proof of a real provider or the owner's credentials.
